## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

Read-only access to the user's Zotero research library. For substantive sport-science questions, build a Zotero-first evidence pack before answering. Return bounded page-located evidence, label external fallback sources explicitly, and never represent a Reference Stub as a reviewed Paper Brief. SecondBrain Queue is the priority lane; promotion eligibility is controlled by promotion_scope.

# 2026-09-20 (closeout) — the map re-ranked, sde_cascade measured off it, backlog cleared

Fourth and final handoff for 2026-09-20. Supersedes
`2026-09-20-apparatus-strip-and-perch-writer.md`, which covers the first half of the
session and is still accurate.

Everything here is merged. No branch is left open except `Weekly_Research_Review`
PR #8, which is open **on purpose** and is the one thing waiting on Eric.

## The through-line worth keeping

Every Jev capability that got **measured** this session moved **down** the map, and
that is now four in a row: entity alignment (withdrawn), PP_Recruiting (rejected),
the Zotero renames (skipped), and today `sde_cascade` (demoted to a code linter). The
pattern is not bad luck, it is a missing gate, and it is now written into
`JEV_CAPABILITY_MAP.md` as one:

> **Build only where all three hold:** the answer is genuinely fuzzy (not a join, a
> threshold or a lookup); something already consumes the answer; and a code baseline
> was measured first.

Each withdrawn item failed a *different* one of the three, which is why no single
check would have caught them.

## What shipped

**TypeSafe_Sandbox** (main `da245ea`, PRs #13–#16 all merged)

- **#13 — the prose-number blind spot is closed.** The planned fix, "strip reference
  sections", was aimed one layer too shallow: removing the bibliography alone leaves
  the citation band at **37, unchanged**. The 49 in-text `[n]` markers were the
  cause. Stripping those too takes the band **37 → 4**, and the planted numeric
  defects from **5 of 6 to 6 of 6**, with **0 false alarms** on review 001's 67 real
  claims and **0 API calls** to prove it.
  - Nearly shipped a first-ever false alarm: the paper writes *"Seven coronal plane
    angles"* and the digit 7 is nowhere in its body, so a truthful "7 angles" deck
    would have been called fabricated. `find_number_word` fixes it; a figure is
    absent only when neither digits nor word appear.
  - A second bug was caught **in review of this PR**: the running-header strip was a
    **silent no-op**, because it anchored its common prefix on page 1 and a title
    page carries extra furniture (`RESEARCH | Article in Press …`). **No test
    failed** — the band is 4 either way. What exposed it was the **byte count not
    reconciling**: the regression printed 29,871 where the table predicted 28,953.
- **#14 — the capability map re-ranked.** Five of fourteen rows closed. The gate
  above added. Next three set as `sde_cascade` → `rerank_typesafe` →
  `composite-scoring`, with `function_calling` demoted to hook-only.
- **#15 — `sde_cascade` measured and demoted.** 10 seeded handoffs, **7.7%
  Jev-shaped** against a pre-registered 25% threshold, **7.7–10.8% across four
  seeds**, 88.4% settled by `stat`/`git`/a file test/a re-run.
  - Bounded in **both** directions after review pointed out a one-sided bound
    flatters the conclusion. Bound A (every ambiguous statement counted as
    Jev-shaped): 16.5%. Bound B (drop code claims whose only evidence is a non-path
    quoted token): 10.4%. **Both at once: 21.6%, and 2 of 4 seeds cross 25%.** So
    "code linter" holds, and **"not a close call" does not** — that phrase was
    removed from every document.
  - "One check covers 85%" was a conflation: 84.9% of code claims carry a backticked
    *token*, but only **39.3%** carry a resolvable *path*.
  - The prototype's real cost is **false alarms, not coverage**: unresolved paths
    walked **43% → 24% without finding one extra file**.
- **#16 — `--pmid` added to the TOS import kit.** See the PR #8 section below; this
  exists because the obvious command does not do what it looks like it does.

**_INBOX** (main `35a7198`, PRs #1 and #2 merged)

- **#1 — `perch.duckdb` is not stale and Windows is writing it.** Last written
  **2026-09-19**, 13,346 rows through `test_date 2026-09-18`, against April's 12,300.
  It cannot have arrived by git: untracked, gitignored, last fetch predated the
  write. The recorded `2026-04-30` was five months stale, so the ownership question
  sat open from 09-13 **on a false premise**.
- **#2 — Windows named the Perch owner**, recorded in `refresh_all_data.bat` next to
  the step it governs, mirroring the GPS block, so the reason is read before the step
  is changed rather than after.

**Weekly_Research_Review** (main `99e7644`, PRs #7 and #10 merged)

- **#7 — the 3-slide executive readout merged**, verified before marking it ready:
  `001` builds all four decks, and `000_sample` with no `readout` block builds
  exactly the two original decks. The additive claim is measured, not assumed.
- **#10 — STATUS rewritten** with the #8 blockage and its four-step unblock.

## The one thing open: PR #8, and why it is not a judgement call yet

`Weekly_Research_Review` **PR #8** (Research in 5 #002, thoracic outlet syndrome)
carries a **DO NOT SEND** flag that has always been a **memory note, never a
measurement.** The verifier built precisely to settle that question **has never been
able to run on it**, and two separate things block it:

1. `reviews/002_thoracic-outlet-overhead/review.json` has an **empty
   `paper.zotero_key`**, and `verify.py` exits immediately without one.
2. **No TOS paper is in Zotero at all** — a library search for "thoracic outlet
   syndrome" returned **zero** records on 2026-09-20.

**The trap, and the reason `--pmid` now exists.** Review 002 runs on
**Funakoshi T, et al. JSES Int 2024;8(3):620-9, PMID 38707577**. That paper is in
`PMIDS_ALL.txt` but is **not** among the priority four in
`verifier/tos_sources/` — those four are the *TOS brief's* misquote sources. So the
documented `import_to_zotero.py --go` unblocks the brief and leaves #002 exactly as
unverifiable as before, while `--go --all` "fixes" it by pushing 109 TOS papers into
a library already being pruned of 25 junk records.

**Unblock sequence, in order:**

1. Eric, with Zotero open, from `TypeSafe_Sandbox`:
   `! python verifier/tos_sources/import_to_zotero.py --go --pmid 38707577`
   (drop `--go` for a dry run; it is tested and returns the record).
2. `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true`; confirm extracted pages, not
   just an abstract.
3. Write the Zotero key into `review.json` as `paper.zotero_key`.
4. Run `tools/verify.ps1` on #002 and let the **result** decide whether it sends.

## Next actions, most important first

1. **The four steps above.** Only step 1 needs Eric; the rest is mechanical.
2. **`rerank_typesafe`** is the map's new #1. Pre-register the test before building:
   ten real past "did we already…?" questions, record the memsearch top-5 hit rate,
   build **only** if it is not already high. Given four consecutive
   measured-it-and-dropped-it results, expect this may not need a build either.
3. **`forceplate.db` ownership** — still open, and unlike Perch it is **genuinely**
   stale (2026-08-02, ingest broken, `pipeline.py` has no `__main__`). Do not carry
   the corrected Perch finding across to it.
4. **Mac follow-up on Perch**: grep launchctl's list for "perch" and stat
   `~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/data/perch.duckdb`. If that box is also
   writing, disable it **there** — Windows holds the credential, the task and the
   fresh DB.
5. **One access conversation unblocks two capability-map items.** `semantic_find`
   needs the Kitman/MyLink contracts (searched: not in `~/DEV`, not on Drive at full
   depth, not in personal Gmail — almost certainly **Baylor Outlook**), and
   `autoresearch_feature_discovery` needs a free-text corpus (the Kitman injury
   export has 29 columns and **no narrative field**; `Pathology` is a controlled
   vocabulary). Both want access, not effort.
6. **Global `MEMORY.md` is stale and at its cap.** It still reads "TypeSafe … NEXT:
   strip ref sections", now three items out of date, at 2,495 of 2,500 characters.
   `memory-write` owns it; consolidate before adding.

## Files created or modified this session

**TypeSafe_Sandbox**
- `verifier/source.py` — apparatus strippers, number words, de-hyphenation, header
  finder; self-test 7 → 17 cases
- `verifier/verify.py` — prose path reads stripped text; selftest 10 → 12 cases
- `verifier/tos_sources/import_to_zotero.py` — `--pmid`
- `verifier/tos_sources/README.md` — the Funakoshi-is-not-in-the-four section
- `sde_cascade/inventory.py` — **new**, the scoping measurement, 23 selftest cases
- `docs/SDE_CASCADE_SCOPING.md` — **new**
- `docs/DELIVERABLE_VERIFIER.md`, `docs/JEV_CAPABILITY_MAP.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`
- `docs/handoffs/2026-09-20-apparatus-strip-and-perch-writer.md` — **new**
- `docs/handoffs/2026-09-20-closeout-capability-map-and-backlog.md` — **new**, this file

**_INBOX**
- `refresh_all_data.bat` — Perch ownership block
- `docs/STATUS.md`

**Weekly_Research_Review**
- `docs/STATUS.md`

## Gotchas carried forward

- **A strip that removes nothing passes every test.** Assert on how much a step
  removed, not only on the headline metric. The header no-op was caught by a byte
  count that did not reconcile across two places.
- **"Strip the references" is the wrong instruction for this problem class.** Strip
  the *apparatus* — bibliography, in-text markers, running headers — and measure the
  band after each.
- **A fallback that lands in a real bucket is a fallback nobody audits.** The
  classifier's default was `opinion`, which swelled it to 46% and hid real claims.
- **A cross-machine linter must know the layout of both boxes** or it reports the
  difference between them as rot. `~/DEV/` is the Mac layout; on Windows DEV is under
  `Desktop`. The SecondBrain vault is Mac-only.
- **CRLF makes identical files look different.** An orphan worktree appeared to have
  17 diverging files; after normalising line endings, **0**.
- **Batch `::` comments must carry no pipes or parentheses** in a file Task Scheduler
  runs unattended. A first draft of the Perch block had both.
- **`0x800710E0` / `2147946720` on a Windows scheduled task is the sleep/power
  signature**, not a script failure. Check the artefact's mtime before concluding a
  job did not run.
- **Checking whether a `.env` exists trips the credential guard if you grep its
  contents.** `ls` plus `git status --ignored` answers it with no secret in scope.
- `verify.py --selftest`, `source.py --self-test` and `inventory.py --selftest` are
  free. `test_verify.py` costs live calls and was **not** run this session.
- On Windows `git worktree remove` fails with Permission denied; `rm -rf` the
  directory then the matching `.git/worktrees/` entry.

331	- **"Is this figure in the paper" is near-useless for small integers — and the cause
332	  is the in-text markers, not the bibliography.** Every integer 0–37 appeared
333	  somewhere in paper 001. Removing the reference section alone leaves that at 37,

337	  remaining range per paper, and the prose check skips integers inside it.
338	- **Narrowing that band without word matching ships a false alarm.** Paper 001 writes
339	  *"Seven coronal plane angles"* and the digit 7 is nowhere in its body, so a deck
340	  truthfully saying "7 angles" would be called fabricated. `source.find_number_word`
341	  covers zero–twenty plus the round tens; absence now means absent in both forms.
342	- **The page extractor leaves a soft hyphen (U+00AD) at every line-break
343	  hyphenation**, so "tenderness" arrives as `ten<U+00AD> derness` and `\bten\b`
344	  matches inside it. Any word-level search over page text must de-hyphenate first —
345	  `source.dehyphenate`. Found by measurement; it made "ten" look present in a paper
346	  that never uses the word.
347	- **Two number-matching rules on purpose.** `find_number` is exact (a table cell
348	  writing 83.9 for the paper's 83.89 is a real misquote). `find_number_rounded` is
349	  prose-only and rounds at the claim's precision (a deck writing "avg age 19.6" for
350	  19.59 is correct). Using the rounded one on a table would ship the misquote —
351	  measured both ways. Do not merge them.
352	- **`ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db` is a DuckDB file, not SQLite.**
353	  Opening it with `sqlite3` raises `file is not a database`, which is almost certainly
354	  all "ForcePlate broken on Windows" ever meant. `duckdb.connect(..., read_only=True)`
355	  opens it fine: 4 tables, 1.25M rows in `raw_tests`. Check the magic bytes before
356	  believing a database is corrupt — this one says `DUCK` at offset 8.
357	- **A Git Bash path like `/g/My Drive/...` is not a path Python can open.** `find`
358	  accepts it and `openpyxl` raises `FileNotFoundError` on the same string. Use the
359	  Windows form `G:\My Drive\...` in Python, the MSYS form in shell tools.
360	- **`except BaseException` around `sys.exit(main())` catches the `SystemExit` that
361	  `sys.exit` itself raises**, so a fail-open wrapper logs an error on every *successful*
362	  run and buries the real failures. Compute the exit code inside the `try`, call
363	  `sys.exit` outside it. Caught by reading the log, which is the argument for having
364	  one: the bug is invisible from the hook's behaviour, since it exits 0 either way.
365	- **A `UserPromptSubmit` hook must never exit non-zero**: exit 2 blocks the prompt.
366	  Fail open means empty stdout and exit 0, always. Watch module-scope code: anything
367	  parsed at import time (an `int()`/`float()` over an env var) runs before the handler
368	  in `__main__` exists and can exit non-zero on its own.
369	- **`urllib`'s `timeout=` is NOT a total deadline.** It applies per blocking socket
370	  operation, so DNS, connect, TLS and every body read each get the whole value. A
371	  server trickling one byte at a time never trips it. For a real wall-clock bound, run
372	  the request on a daemon thread and `join(remaining)`; the daemon flag is what lets
373	  the process exit while the socket is still wedged.
374	- `~/.claude/hooks/hooks.json` is NOT live. It carries a full `UserPromptSubmit` block
375	  (`TheRouter.hook.ts` and friends, bun-based, with Mac paths), but nothing in
376	  `settings.json` references it. Do not assume a hook runs because it is written down.
377	- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
378	  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
379	- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
380	  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
381	  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
382	- A restart of Claude Code matters only for things that inherit Claude Code's own
383	  environment, such as the plugin / MCP processes. The Bash tool does NOT need it:
384	  it spawns a fresh zsh, which sources `~/.zshenv` and picks the key up. Verified
385	  2026-09-19 with `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" /bin/zsh -c 'echo ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}'`
386	  -> `set`. Pass `USER`: the `.zshenv` line calls `security ... -a "$USER"`.
387	- **The key needs its `apikey_` prefix.** The console shows `apikey_<36>_<64>`, 108 characters
388	  total. Pasting only the part after `apikey_` returns a clean `401 authentication_error` from
389	  `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. A malformed request body returns 422 instead,
390	  so 401 means the key value is wrong and 422 means your request is wrong. That split is the
391	  fastest way to tell which end is at fault.
392	- **Windows home for the key is `~/.claude/typesafe.env`**, one line,
393	  `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=apikey_...`. That path is auto-gitignored by the dotclaude whitelist
394	  (`.gitignore` line 5 is `/*`, so any new top-level file there is ignored), and Claude reads
395	  it directly with no restart.
396	- **`~/.bashrc` is NOT sourced by Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows.** Tested with a probe
397	  export: not visible in a fresh tool shell. Do not put env vars there expecting the agent to
398	  see them.
399	- **Windows user environment variables ARE inherited** by the agent's shell, so
400	  `setx NAME "value"` plus a Claude Code restart also works. That is how `FIREFLIES_API_KEY`
401	  and the GitHub PAT already reach it. Use it if you want the variable set automatically
402	  rather than read from a file.
403	- **`.claude/` is gitignored here.** Claude Code puts per-project worktrees in
404	  `.claude/worktrees/`, so without the ignore a `git add -A` would commit a whole nested
405	  checkout. A locked worktree (`jev-docs-capability-map`) was live in there on 2026-09-19.
406	- On Windows, `git worktree remove` and `git worktree prune` often fail with
407	  "Permission denied" on the first try because of a transient file lock. A plain `rm -rf` of
408	  the same path immediately afterwards succeeds. Remove the directory, then the matching
409	  entry under `.git/worktrees/`.
410	- Verified 2026-09-19 on Windows against the live API: on a hamstring-tightness note, Noul
411	  0.9 for "possible injury", Choice "lower body", Score 1.69 across
412	  ["monitor only", "modify training", "hold out"]. All three primitives return sane values.

## Gotchas
- **"Is this figure in the paper" is near-useless for small integers — and the cause
  is the in-text markers, not the bibliography.** Every integer 0–37 appeared
  somewhere in paper 001. Removing the reference section alone leaves that at 37,
  exactly unchanged; removing the 49 `[n]` markers in the body takes it to 4.
  Measured 2026-09-20, after an earlier note in this file asserted the opposite.
  `source.body_pages` strips the apparatus, `source.citation_band` derives the
  remaining range per paper, and the prose check skips integers inside it.
- **Narrowing that band without word matching ships a false alarm.** Paper 001 writes
  *"Seven coronal plane angles"* and the digit 7 is nowhere in its body, so a deck
  truthfully saying "7 angles" would be called fabricated. `source.find_number_word`
  covers zero–twenty plus the round tens; absence now means absent in both forms.
- **The page extractor leaves a soft hyphen (U+00AD) at every line-break
  hyphenation**, so "tenderness" arrives as `ten<U+00AD> derness` and `\bten\b`
  matches inside it. Any word-level search over page text must de-hyphenate first —
  `source.dehyphenate`. Found by measurement; it made "ten" look present in a paper
  that never uses the word.
- **Two number-matching rules on purpose.** `find_number` is exact (a table cell
  writing 83.9 for the paper's 83.89 is a real misquote). `find_number_rounded` is
  prose-only and rounds at the claim's precision (a deck writing "avg age 19.6" for
  19.59 is correct). Using the rounded one on a table would ship the misquote —
  measured both ways. Do not merge them.
- **`ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db` is a DuckDB file, not SQLite.**
  Opening it with `sqlite3` raises `file is not a database`, which is almost certainly
  all "ForcePlate broken on Windows" ever meant. `duckdb.connect(..., read_only=True)`
  opens it fine: 4 tables, 1.25M rows in `raw_tests`. Check the magic bytes before
  believing a database is corrupt — this one says `DUCK` at offset 8.
- **A Git Bash path like `/g/My Drive/...` is not a path Python can open.** `find`
  accepts it and `openpyxl` raises `FileNotFoundError` on the same string. Use the
  Windows form `G:\My Drive\...` in Python, the MSYS form in shell tools.
- **`except BaseException` around `sys.exit(main())` catches the `SystemExit` that
  `sys.exit` itself raises**, so a fail-open wrapper logs an error on every *successful*
  run and buries the real failures. Compute the exit code inside the `try`, call
  `sys.exit` outside it. Caught by reading the log, which is the argument for having
  one: the bug is invisible from the hook's behaviour, since it exits 0 either way.
- **A `UserPromptSubmit` hook must never exit non-zero**: exit 2 blocks the prompt.
  Fail open means empty stdout and exit 0, always. Watch module-scope code: anything
  parsed at import time (an `int()`/`float()` over an env var) runs before the handler
  in `__main__` exists and can exit non-zero on its own.
- **`urllib`'s `timeout=` is NOT a total deadline.** It applies per blocking socket
  operation, so DNS, connect, TLS and every body read each get the whole value. A
  server trickling one byte at a time never trips it. For a real wall-clock bound, run
  the request on a daemon thread and `join(remaining)`; the daemon flag is what lets
  the process exit while the socket is still wedged.
- `~/.claude/hooks/hooks.json` is NOT live. It carries a full `UserPromptSubmit` block
  (`TheRouter.hook.ts` and friends, bun-based, with Mac paths), but nothing in
  `settings.json` references it. Do not assume a hook runs because it is written down.
- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
- A restart of Claude Code matters only for things that inherit Claude Code's own
  environment, such as the plugin / MCP processes. The Bash tool does NOT need it:
  it spawns a fresh zsh, which sources `~/.zshenv` and picks the key up. Verified
  2026-09-19 with `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" /bin/zsh -c 'echo ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}'`
  -> `set`. Pass `USER`: the `.zshenv` line calls `security ... -a "$USER"`.
- **The key needs its `apikey_` prefix.** The console shows `apikey_<36>_<64>`, 108 characters
  total. Pasting only the part after `apikey_` returns a clean `401 authentication_error` from
  `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. A malformed request body returns 422 instead,
  so 401 means the key value is wrong and 422 means your request is wrong. That split is the
  fastest way to tell which end is at fault.
- **Windows home for the key is `~/.claude/typesafe.env`**, one line,
  `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=apikey_...`. That path is auto-gitignored by the dotclaude whitelist
  (`.gitignore` line 5 is `/*`, so any new top-level file there is ignored), and Claude reads
  it directly with no restart.
- **`~/.bashrc` is NOT sourced by Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows.** Tested with a probe
  export: not visible in a fresh tool shell. Do not put env vars there expecting the agent to
  see them.
- **Windows user environment variables ARE inherited** by the agent's shell, so
  `setx NAME "value"` plus a Claude Code restart also works. That is how `FIREFLIES_API_KEY`
  and the GitHub PAT already reach it. Use it if you want the variable set automatically
  rather than read from a file.
- **`.claude/` is gitignored here.** Claude Code puts per-project worktrees in
  `.claude/worktrees/`, so without the ignore a `git add -A` would commit a whole nested
  checkout. A locked worktree (`jev-docs-capability-map`) was live in there on 2026-09-19.
- On Windows, `git worktree remove` and `git worktree prune` often fail with
  "Permission denied" on the first try because of a transient file lock. A plain `rm -rf` of
  the same path immediately afterwards succeeds. Remove the directory, then the matching
  entry under `.git/worktrees/`.
- Verified 2026-09-19 on Windows against the live API: on a hamstring-tightness note, Noul
  0.9 for "possible injury", Choice "lower body", Score 1.69 across
  ["monitor only", "modify training", "hold out"]. All three primitives return sane values.

# AGENTS.md

Project: TypeSafe_Sandbox

## What this is
A sandbox for building against the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model), which
returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo; see Secrets below for where it lives on each machine.
`setup_global_key.sh` installs the macOS side once per machine. `smoke_test.py` proves
the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

## Secrets
- Never paste the API key into a chat session. Claude Code transcripts under
  `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are tracked in the `dotclaude` repo and pushed nightly.
- Never put the key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`. Both are tracked.
- The key has one home per machine, and nothing about it syncs between them:
  - macOS: the Keychain, service name `typesafe-api-key`, installed by `setup_global_key.sh`.
  - Windows: `~/.claude/typesafe.env`, which the dotclaude whitelist auto-ignores.
- The key is 108 characters and starts with `apikey_`. Dropping that prefix returns 401.

I read the closeout handoff, `STATUS.md` and the capability map's "Next three" section. Several items on the backlog are just chores: the Mac Perch check, consolidating `MEMORY.md`, and steps 2–4 of the PR #8 unblock. The list below is only the decisions that are yours to make, most important first.

## 1. Does TypeSafe stay an active project?
This is the biggest decision, and nobody has put it to you directly. Four capabilities were measured in a row, and all four dropped down the map. Two things actually earn their keep: the skill router and the verifier. The rest of the map is either blocked on access (`semantic_find`, `autoresearch`) or marginal (`rerank`, `composite-scoring`). STATUS also notes that TypeSafe got built without taking one of the 5 slate slots, and says whether the slate needs re-cutting is your call.

**My recommendation:** run the one cheap `rerank_typesafe` test, then move TypeSafe to maintenance mode: keep the router and the verifier, and stop looking for new uses of Jev. The gate you wrote says to build where the problem is, and you're currently doing the reverse: starting from Jev and hunting for problems.

## 2. PR #8 (TOS #002): decide what the result will mean before you run it
Step 1 is still your command: `! python verifier/tos_sources/import_to_zotero.py --go --pmid 38707577`, with Zotero open. The decision underneath it is whether the verifier's verdict binds you:
- If it comes back clean, does #002 send, even though "DO NOT SEND" has been in your head for days?
- If it flags claims, do you fix the review or kill it?

Decide now, the same way you pre-register a threshold. Otherwise the tool gets overruled by the memory note it was built to test.

There's also a separate call: whether to import the TOS brief's four priority papers. That brief is the known-bad case and the verifier's best test, but the import writes into a library you're in the middle of pruning.

## 3. Should the verifier gate sends?
Nothing calls `verify.py` yet. Wiring it into `/research-in-5` or `build.js` means a failing claim blocks a send. That's a policy decision: who can override the block, and how. It isn't a code question.

## 4. The access conversation, and a challenge to it
The handoff frames Baylor Outlook (for the contracts) plus a Kitman key that isn't read-only (for narrative fields) as one conversation that unblocks two items. I'd push back on the first half. Kitman vs MyLink is holding up priority 3, and it's a question about a few contracts. That's a lookup, which fails condition 1 of your own gate. **Read the contracts yourself and make the call.** Don't let a Jev build sit between you and a purchasing decision. The Kitman narrative-field access is the half worth asking for, but only if a free-text field actually exists. The current export has none.

## 5. Who owns `forceplate.db`, and when does the ingest get fixed?
Unlike Perch, this one really is stale. It was last written 2026-08-02, the ingest is broken, and `pipeline.py` has no `__main__`. You need to pick an owner box, and pick between fixing it mid-season and parking it until the off-season. Given "nothing that breaks mid-season", park it unless someone is actively using force-plate numbers right now.

## 6. Skill router: keep it, extend it to the Mac, or roll it back?
The first 500 characters of every prompt go to `api.typesafe.ai`. You accepted that trade-off, but it hasn't been revisited since, and the log sample from 09-19 was small. There are three options:
- Keep it on Windows only.
- Enable it on the Mac. That needs its own roster rebuild first.
- Roll it back by deleting one settings key.

## 7. Two smaller calls
- **`composite-scoring`:** the only valid test uses the full project registry, since the 5-item slate proves nothing. Otherwise skip it. I'd skip it.
- **Zotero write key:** both the 25 junk deletions and the TOS imports need write access. Decide whether this machine gets a write key or whether you do those by hand.

If you want to work through these one at a time, #1 is the place to start, because its answer settles #4 and #7 and most of #6.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Import the TOS brief's source papers into Zotero, via the running app.

Why this script exists rather than Claude just doing it: the Zotero WEB key on this
machine is read-only (`write: false`), and Claude's sandbox refuses POSTs to local
services ("External System Writes"). Zotero being open opens a path that is genuinely
different - the connector endpoint the browser extension uses - but it has to be run
by Eric, not by the agent. This is that one command.

    python import_to_zotero.py            # dry run: fetch, show, write nothing
    python import_to_zotero.py --go       # actually import into Zotero
    python import_to_zotero.py --go --all # all 109, not just the priority four
    python import_to_zotero.py --go --pmid 38707577   # one paper, by PMID

Zotero must be open. Nothing here touches the web API or syncs anything; it hands
metadata to the local app exactly as the browser connector does, and Zotero then does
its own thing with it, including trying for an open-access PDF when it can.

AFTER importing, two more steps matter, because metadata alone does not help:

  1. Attach the PDFs. The verifier reads page-level text; an item with no PDF is
     still unusable to it. Behind a paywall this needs the Baylor proxy, i.e. you.
  2. Re-index: `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true`, then check with
     `python ../source.py <item key>` - it should list pages.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CONNECTOR = "http://127.0.0.1:23119/connector"
EFETCH = (
    "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi"
    "?db=pubmed&rettype=medline&retmode=text&id={ids}"
)

PRIORITY = {
    "40673787": "Kamarajugadda - misquote 1, exceedance rate read as volume share",
    "36003968": "Takaba - misquote 2, 53% increase called 'roughly doubles'",
    "39844736": "Ulman - misquote 3, 49.9% variance misattributed",
    "40132734": "Talutis - the denominator the statistical section needs",
}


def fetch(pmids: list[str]) -> str:
    """MEDLINE records for these PMIDs, in one polite request."""
    url = EFETCH.format(ids=",".join(pmids))
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url, headers={"User-Agent": "TypeSafe_Sandbox TOS import (one-off)"}
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        return response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

# rerank_typesafe: measure before building

Map item #2 after `sde_cascade` was measured off it. This file is written **before**
any question is scored, so the decision rule cannot be fitted to the result.

## What exists today (the code baseline)

- memsearch over Milvus, embedding `gpahal/bge-m3-onnx-int8` (local ONNX).
- `[reranker] model = ""`: **no reranker is configured.** memsearch already ships a
  `--reranker-model` cross-encoder option, so a free local reranker is the code
  baseline any Jev reranker has to beat (gate condition 3).
- Index on 2026-09-21: 15,595 chunks. dev-docs mirrors 9,775, transcripts 3,383,
  compiled knowledge 1,456, daily logs 385, Tier A memory and Codex memories the rest.

## Pre-registered test

1. **Ten real recall questions**, taken from Eric's own past prompts in the session
   transcripts ("did we already…", "what did we decide…", "do you remember…"),
   collected newest-first and not chosen for ease. Each question gets its ground
   truth, the file that holds the answer, from the transcript's own reply and a grep.
   **Ground truth is never found using memsearch**, because that would be circular.
2. Run `memsearch search "<question>" -k 20` exactly as the question was asked.
3. Record **hit@5** (the answer file is in the top 5) and **hit@20**.

## Decision rule, fixed in advance

- **hit@5 ≥ 8 of 10**: do not build. Retrieval is already good enough, and this is
  the Zotero-renames trap.
- **Misses that are not in the top 20 either**: a reranker cannot fix them, because it
  only reorders what comes back. Those are an indexing or coverage problem, and they
  count **against** building.
- **Build only if at least 3 misses sit in positions 6 to 20.** Even then, try
  memsearch's own local cross-encoder first, and only reach for Jev if that leaves at
  least 2 of those misses unfixed.

## Result

# verify.ps1 - check a review against the paper it reports, before it is sent.
#
#   pwsh tools/verify.ps1 reviews/001_alignment-jumpers-knee
#
# Wraps the deliverable verifier, which lives in the TypeSafe_Sandbox repo rather than
# here: it is shared tooling and a second copy would drift. This script's whole job is
# to find it, run it, and translate its exit code into this project's PASS / FAIL /
# DEGRADED vocabulary.
#
# Exit codes, which publish.ps1 depends on:
#   0  PASS      every claim checked out, or the only opinions were `review` items
#   1  FAIL      a claim is fabricated, contradicted, unsupported, or on the wrong page
#   2  DEGRADED  the verifier could not run at all
#
# DEGRADED DOES NOT BLOCK A PUBLISH, and that is deliberate. The verifier needs the
# TypeSafe_Sandbox clone, a built venv, an API key and a network. Eric works on two
# machines and the Mac has no PowerPoint either; a check that blocks the week's
# deliverable because a sibling repo is missing is a check that gets deleted. It is
# loud instead, and WORKFLOW.md says a DEGRADED verify must be reported the same way a
# DEGRADED image QA is. A real finding, by contrast, does block.
#
# Override the location if TypeSafe_Sandbox is somewhere unusual:
#   $env:RI5_VERIFIER = "D:\somewhere\TypeSafe_Sandbox\verifier\verify.py"

param(
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Review
)

$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot

# Walk up looking for the DEV directory that holds TypeSafe_Sandbox, rather than
# assuming it is one level above this repo. It usually is - but AGENTS.md tells a
# background session to work in `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, and from there the parent
# is `.claude/worktrees`, not DEV. Assuming the depth would break the check in exactly
# the setup this project runs in most often.
function Find-Sandbox($from) {
  $dir = $from
  for ($i = 0; $i -lt 8 -and $dir; $i++) {
    $candidate = Join-Path $dir "TypeSafe_Sandbox\verifier\verify.py"
    if (Test-Path $candidate) { return $candidate }
    $dir = Split-Path -Parent $dir
  }
  return $null
}

function Write-Degraded($reason) {
  Write-Host "VERIFY DEGRADED - $reason" -ForegroundColor Yellow
  Write-Host "      The deck was NOT checked against its paper. Say so when reporting QA."
  Write-Host "      Setup: TypeSafe_Sandbox needs a venv and ~/.claude/typesafe.env."
  exit 2
}

# 1. Find verify.py.
$verifier = $env:RI5_VERIFIER
if (-not $verifier) { $verifier = Find-Sandbox $root }
if (-not $verifier -or -not (Test-Path $verifier)) {
  Write-Degraded "no TypeSafe_Sandbox/verifier/verify.py above $root"
}

# 2. Find the interpreter. Prefer that repo's own venv, which is where its deps live;
#    a bare `python` usually cannot import them.
$sandbox = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $verifier)
$python = Join-Path $sandbox ".venv\Scripts\python.exe"
if (-not (Test-Path $python)) { $python = Join-Path $sandbox ".venv/bin/python" }
if (-not (Test-Path $python)) {
  $python = (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source
  if (-not $python) { Write-Degraded "no python found for the verifier" }
}

# 3. The review.json to check.
$json = Join-Path $root (Join-Path $Review "review.json")
if (-not (Test-Path $json)) { $json = Join-Path $Review "review.json" }
if (-not (Test-Path $json)) { Write-Degraded "no review.json under $Review" }

Write-Host "VERIFY checking $(Split-Path -Leaf (Split-Path -Parent $json)) against its paper"
$output = & $python $verifier --review $json 2>&1
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$output | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }

# A clean deck and one carrying seven items a person still has to read both exit 0.
# Collapsing them both to "PASS" would quietly retire the uncertain band, which is the
# part of the design doing the most work: `review` means the model was not confident
# enough to decide, so a human decides instead. Say how many.
$pending = ([regex]::Matches(($output -join "`n"), '(?m)^\s*\[REVIEW\]')).Count

# The verifier exits 1 for a real finding. It raises on a missing key or an
# unreachable API, which surfaces as a non-zero code too, so separate the two by
# whether it managed to print a verdict: no verdict means it never got started.
if ($code -eq 0) {
  if ($pending -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "VERIFY PASS - $pending claim(s) need a human read before sending" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "      These are the [REVIEW] lines above. The model was not confident"
    Write-Host "      enough to decide; check them against notes.md yourself."
  } else {
    Write-Host "VERIFY PASS - every claim checked out" -ForegroundColor Green
  }
  exit 0
}
if ($code -eq 1) {
  Write-Host "VERIFY FAIL - a claim does not match the paper. Do not send." -ForegroundColor Red
  Write-Host "      Fix review.json, rebuild, and verify again."
  exit 1
}
Write-Degraded "verifier exited $code before reaching a verdict"

# publish.ps1 - build, export, index, and copy one review to Google Drive.
#
#   pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/001_sleep-extension          # full run
#   pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/001_sleep-extension -NoDrive # local only (QA)
#   pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/001_sleep-extension -SkipVerify  # bypass the gate
#
# A full run verifies the deck against its paper before copying to Drive and refuses
# on a real finding. See tools/verify.ps1. -NoDrive does not verify; step 5 of
# WORKFLOW.md runs the check explicitly during QA.
#
# Steps: node build.js (light + dark decks) -> PowerPoint COM export of each deck
#        (PDF + slide PNGs for QA) -> font check -> node index.js -> copy to Drive.
# PowerPoint must not be mid-dialog; close open decks first if COM export fails.

param(
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Review,
  [switch]$NoDrive,
  [switch]$SkipVerify
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$drive = "G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5"

Push-Location $root
try {
  if (-not (Test-Path "node_modules\pptxgenjs")) { npm install --silent | Out-Null }

  node tools/build.js $Review
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "build.js failed; see errors above." }

  $folder = Split-Path -Leaf (Resolve-Path $Review)
  $out = Join-Path $root "build\$folder"
  $manifest = Get-Content (Join-Path $out "last-build.json") -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
  $pdfs = @()

  $pp = New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application
  try {
    foreach ($d in $manifest.decks) {
      $pptx = Join-Path $out $d.pptx
      $pdf = [IO.Path]::ChangeExtension($pptx, ".pdf")
      Remove-Item "$out\$($d.theme)-slide*.png" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
      # Open(path, ReadOnly, Untitled, WithWindow)
      $deck = $pp.Presentations.Open($pptx, $true, $false, $false)
      $deck.SaveAs($pdf, 32)  # 32 = ppSaveAsPDF
      foreach ($s in $deck.Slides) { $s.Export("$out\$($d.theme)-slide$($s.SlideIndex).png", "PNG", 1500, 844) }
      $deck.Close()
      $pdfs += $pdf

      # Font check. Agency FB must be embedded or Teams viewers get a substitute.
      # Do not treat Calibri as a fallback: PowerPoint cannot embed Baylor Bears (an
      # OpenType-CFF font), so it draws Bears text as outlines and labels the hidden
      # text layer Calibri. build.js keeps unsupported characters out of Bears text.
      $bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($pdf, [Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591))
      $agency = $bytes -match '/BaseFont\s*/[A-Z]{6}\+AgencyFB'
      Write-Host ("PDF   {0}" -f (Split-Path -Leaf $pdf))
      Write-Host ("      Agency FB embedded: {0}" -f $agency)
      Write-Host "      PNGs: $out\$($d.theme)-slide1..5.png"
    }
  } finally {
    if ($pp.Presentations.Count -eq 0) { $pp.Quit() }
    [void][Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ReleaseComObject($pp)
  }

  node tools/index.js
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "index.js failed." }

  # Check the deck against its paper before anything reaches Drive. This sits on the
  # publish path rather than the QA path because copying to Drive is the point of no
  # return: from there Eric attaches the PDF to a Teams post and an email. A -NoDrive
  # QA run stays fast and unverified on purpose; WORKFLOW.md step 5 runs the check
  # explicitly so problems surface before the images are read, not after.
  #
  # Only a real finding blocks. A verifier that cannot run (exit 2) warns and lets the
  # publish through - see tools/verify.ps1 for why that is deliberate.
  if (-not $NoDrive -and -not $SkipVerify) {
    & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "verify.ps1") $Review
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 1) {
      throw "Verification FAILED: a claim does not match the paper. Nothing was copied to Drive. Fix review.json and rerun, or pass -SkipVerify if you have checked it by hand."
    }
  }

  if (-not $NoDrive) {
    $dest = Join-Path $drive $folder
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dest | Out-Null
    $files = @($manifest.decks | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $out $_.pptx }) + $pdfs + @((Join-Path $out $manifest.teams), (Join-Path $out $manifest.email))
    foreach ($f in $files) { Copy-Item -LiteralPath $f -Destination $dest -Force }
    Copy-Item "$root\build\Research_in_5_Index.csv" $drive -Force
    Write-Host "Drive $dest"
  }
} finally {
  Pop-Location
}

  $python = (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source
  if (-not $python) { Write-Degraded "no python found for the verifier" }
}

# 3. The review.json to check.
$json = Join-Path $root (Join-Path $Review "review.json")
if (-not (Test-Path $json)) { $json = Join-Path $Review "review.json" }
if (-not (Test-Path $json)) { Write-Degraded "no review.json under $Review" }

Write-Host "VERIFY checking $(Split-Path -Leaf (Split-Path -Parent $json)) against its paper"
$output = & $python $verifier --review $json 2>&1
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$output | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }

# A clean deck and one carrying seven items a person still has to read both exit 0.
# Collapsing them both to "PASS" would quietly retire the uncertain band, which is the
# part of the design doing the most work: `review` means the model was not confident
# enough to decide, so a human decides instead. Say how many.
$pending = ([regex]::Matches(($output -join "`n"), '(?m)^\s*\[REVIEW\]')).Count

# The verifier exits 1 for a real finding. It raises on a missing key or an
# unreachable API, which surfaces as a non-zero code too, so separate the two by
# whether it managed to print a verdict: no verdict means it never got started.
if ($code -eq 0) {
  if ($pending -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "VERIFY PASS - $pending claim(s) need a human read before sending" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "      These are the [REVIEW] lines above. The model was not confident"
    Write-Host "      enough to decide; check them against notes.md yourself."
  } else {
    Write-Host "VERIFY PASS - every claim checked out" -ForegroundColor Green
  }
  exit 0
}
if ($code -eq 1) {
  Write-Host "VERIFY FAIL - a claim does not match the paper. Do not send." -ForegroundColor Red
  Write-Host "      Fix review.json, rebuild, and verify again."
  exit 1
}

# publish.ps1 - build, export, index, and copy one review to Google Drive.
#
#   pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/001_sleep-extension          # full run
#   pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/001_sleep-extension -NoDrive # local only (QA)
#   pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/001_sleep-extension -SkipVerify  # bypass the gate
#
# A full run verifies the deck against its paper before copying to Drive and refuses
# on a real finding. See tools/verify.ps1. -NoDrive does not verify; step 5 of
# WORKFLOW.md runs the check explicitly during QA.
#
# Steps: node build.js (light + dark decks) -> PowerPoint COM export of each deck
#        (PDF + slide PNGs for QA) -> font check -> node index.js -> copy to Drive.
# PowerPoint must not be mid-dialog; close open decks first if COM export fails.

param(
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Review,
  [switch]$NoDrive,
  [switch]$SkipVerify
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$drive = "G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5"

Push-Location $root
try {
  if (-not (Test-Path "node_modules\pptxgenjs")) { npm install --silent | Out-Null }

  node tools/build.js $Review
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "build.js failed; see errors above." }

  $folder = Split-Path -Leaf (Resolve-Path $Review)
  $out = Join-Path $root "build\$folder"
  $manifest = Get-Content (Join-Path $out "last-build.json") -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
  $pdfs = @()

  $pp = New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application
  try {
    foreach ($d in $manifest.decks) {
      $pptx = Join-Path $out $d.pptx
      $pdf = [IO.Path]::ChangeExtension($pptx, ".pdf")
      Remove-Item "$out\$($d.theme)-slide*.png" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
      # Open(path, ReadOnly, Untitled, WithWindow)
      $deck = $pp.Presentations.Open($pptx, $true, $false, $false)
      $deck.SaveAs($pdf, 32)  # 32 = ppSaveAsPDF
      foreach ($s in $deck.Slides) { $s.Export("$out\$($d.theme)-slide$($s.SlideIndex).png", "PNG", 1500, 844) }
      $deck.Close()
      $pdfs += $pdf

      # Font check. Agency FB must be embedded or Teams viewers get a substitute.
      # Do not treat Calibri as a fallback: PowerPoint cannot embed Baylor Bears (an
      # OpenType-CFF font), so it draws Bears text as outlines and labels the hidden
      # text layer Calibri. build.js keeps unsupported characters out of Bears text.
      $bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($pdf, [Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591))
      $agency = $bytes -match '/BaseFont\s*/[A-Z]{6}\+AgencyFB'
      Write-Host ("PDF   {0}" -f (Split-Path -Leaf $pdf))
      Write-Host ("      Agency FB embedded: {0}" -f $agency)
      Write-Host "      PNGs: $out\$($d.theme)-slide1..5.png"
    }
  } finally {
    if ($pp.Presentations.Count -eq 0) { $pp.Quit() }
    [void][Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ReleaseComObject($pp)
  }

  node tools/index.js
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "index.js failed." }

  # Check the deck against its paper before anything reaches Drive. This sits on the
  # publish path rather than the QA path because copying to Drive is the point of no
  # return: from there Eric attaches the PDF to a Teams post and an email. A -NoDrive
  # QA run stays fast and unverified on purpose; WORKFLOW.md step 5 runs the check
  # explicitly so problems surface before the images are read, not after.
  #
  # Only a real finding blocks. A verifier that cannot run (exit 2) warns and lets the
  # publish through - see tools/verify.ps1 for why that is deliberate.
  if (-not $NoDrive -and -not $SkipVerify) {
    & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "verify.ps1") $Review
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 1) {
      throw "Verification FAILED: a claim does not match the paper. Nothing was copied to Drive. Fix review.json and rerun, or pass -SkipVerify if you have checked it by hand."
    }
  }

  if (-not $NoDrive) {
    $dest = Join-Path $drive $folder
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dest | Out-Null
    $files = @($manifest.decks | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $out $_.pptx }) + $pdfs + @((Join-Path $out $manifest.teams), (Join-Path $out $manifest.email))
    foreach ($f in $files) { Copy-Item -LiteralPath $f -Destination $dest -Force }
    Copy-Item "$root\build\Research_in_5_Index.csv" $drive -Force
    Write-Host "Drive $dest"
  }
} finally {
  Pop-Location
}

# rerank_typesafe: measure before building

Map item #2 after `sde_cascade` was measured off it. This file is written **before**
any question is scored, so the decision rule cannot be fitted to the result.

## What exists today (the code baseline)

- memsearch over Milvus, embedding `gpahal/bge-m3-onnx-int8` (local ONNX).
- `[reranker] model = ""`: **no reranker is configured.** memsearch already ships a
  `--reranker-model` cross-encoder option, so a free local reranker is the code
  baseline any Jev reranker has to beat (gate condition 3).
- Index on 2026-09-21: 15,595 chunks. dev-docs mirrors 9,775, transcripts 3,383,
  compiled knowledge 1,456, daily logs 385, Tier A memory and Codex memories the rest.

## Pre-registered test

1. **Ten real recall questions**, taken from Eric's own past prompts in the session
   transcripts ("did we already…", "what did we decide…", "do you remember…"),
   collected newest-first and not chosen for ease. Each question gets its ground
   truth, the file that holds the answer, from the transcript's own reply and a grep.
   **Ground truth is never found using memsearch**, because that would be circular.
2. Run `memsearch search "<question>" -k 20` exactly as the question was asked.
3. Record **hit@5** (the answer file is in the top 5) and **hit@20**.

## Decision rule, fixed in advance

- **hit@5 ≥ 8 of 10**: do not build. Retrieval is already good enough, and this is
  the Zotero-renames trap.
- **Misses that are not in the top 20 either**: a reranker cannot fix them, because it
  only reorders what comes back. Those are an indexing or coverage problem, and they
  count **against** building.
- **Build only if at least 3 misses sit in positions 6 to 20.** Even then, try
  memsearch's own local cross-encoder first, and only reach for Jev if that leaves at
  least 2 of those misses unfixed.

"""Score memsearch against pre-registered recall questions. See docs/RERANK_MEASUREMENT.md.

    python rerank_measure/score.py rerank_measure/questions.json [--reranker MODEL]

A hit is a chunk, not a file: its source is one of the question's answer files AND
its text contains at least half of the answer keywords (case-insensitive). Coverage
is checked first, against the Milvus `source` field, so an answer that was never
indexed is reported as a coverage miss rather than a ranking miss.

Local only. memsearch embeds with an on-box ONNX model; nothing here calls TypeSafe.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from pymilvus import MilvusClient

K = 20


def norm(path: str) -> str:
    return path.replace("\\", "/").lower().rstrip("/")


def indexed_sources() -> set[str]:
    client = MilvusClient("http://localhost:19530")
    rows = client.query("memsearch_chunks", filter="", output_fields=["source"], limit=16384)
    return {norm(r["source"]) for r in rows}


def search(question: str, reranker: str | None) -> list[dict]:
    cmd = ["memsearch", "search", question, "-k", str(K), "-j"]
    if reranker is not None:
        cmd += ["--reranker-model", reranker]
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    return json.loads(out.stdout)


def is_hit(chunk: dict, answer_files: set[str], keywords: list[str]) -> bool:
    if norm(chunk.get("source", "")) not in answer_files:
        return False
    text = (chunk.get("content") or chunk.get("text") or "").lower()
    found = sum(1 for k in keywords if k.lower() in text)
    return found * 2 >= len(keywords)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("questions")
    parser.add_argument("--reranker", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    questions = json.loads(Path(args.questions).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    sources = indexed_sources()
    rows = []
    for q in questions:
        files = {norm(f) for f in q["answer_files"]}
        covered = bool(files & sources)
        rank = None
        if covered:
            for i, chunk in enumerate(search(q["question"], args.reranker), start=1):
                if is_hit(chunk, files, q["answer_keywords"]):
                    rank = i
                    break
        rows.append({"id": q["id"], "covered": covered, "rank": rank,
                     "question": q["question"][:70]})

    for r in rows:
        where = "NOT INDEXED" if not r["covered"] else (f"rank {r['rank']}" if r["rank"] else f"miss@{K}")
        print(f"{r['id']:>4}  {where:<12} {r['question']}")
    hit5 = sum(1 for r in rows if r["rank"] and r["rank"] <= 5)
    hit20 = sum(1 for r in rows if r["rank"])
    band = sum(1 for r in rows if r["rank"] and r["rank"] > 5)
    uncovered = sum(1 for r in rows if not r["covered"])
    print(f"\nhit@5 {hit5}/{len(rows)}   hit@{K} {hit20}/{len(rows)}   "
          f"ranks 6-{K} {band}   not indexed {uncovered}")
    json.dump(rows, sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

The scoring script is written. Its field names match memsearch's JSON output (`content`, `source`). Both background agents are still running, so here are answers to the two questions you asked.

## #2: Where to run the import
Run it in this Claude Code prompt, prefixed with `!`, with the **Zotero desktop app open**:

```
! cd ~/Desktop/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox && python verifier/tos_sources/import_to_zotero.py --pmid 38707577
```

That's a dry run: it fetches the PubMed record and writes nothing. If it shows Funakoshi (JSES Int 2024), run it again with `--go` to import.

It has to be you rather than me for two reasons. It posts to the Zotero app's local connector at `127.0.0.1:23119`, and my sandbox blocks writes to local services. And the Zotero web key on this machine is read-only. A `!` command runs as you, outside the sandbox.

Metadata alone isn't enough. After the import, check that the PDF is attached to the item. JSES International is open access, so Zotero may attach it automatically; if not, add it. Once it's attached, I handle the re-sync, write the key into `review.json`, and run the verifier.

## #4: What Outlook or Kitman access would be for
Honestly, I don't need either one.
- **Outlook:** the Kitman and MyLink contracts are probably sitting in your Baylor email. The capability map wanted them as a test corpus for a Jev "ask the contract a question" tool (`semantic_find`). But choosing between Kitman and MyLink means reading two or three contracts, which you can do in an afternoon. Building a tool for that fails the first condition of your gate: it's a lookup, not a fuzzy judgement. **You need the contracts to make the call; TypeSafe doesn't.**
- **Kitman:** the idea was a key that exposes free-text injury or clinical notes, which Jev could turn into model features. The export we already have has 29 columns and no narrative field at all. So this access request rests on a corpus we haven't confirmed exists. Only ask if you already know Kitman stores prose notes.

I'm dropping both from the TypeSafe backlog. Kitman vs MyLink stays on your pending-decisions list as your call, with no Jev tool in front of it.

## #3: A correction and a decision
I was wrong earlier. The verifier is already a send gate: `publish.ps1` runs it before anything is copied to Drive, and `-SkipVerify` is the override. What I found instead is a bug. A review with no Zotero key, which is exactly #002's state, gets reported as "a claim does not match the paper" when nothing was compared at all. My decision: it **keeps blocking**, but the message will say "could not check this deck" and give the reason. An agent is fixing that in `Weekly_Research_Review` now and will open a PR.

## #1: Rerank test
The pass/fail rule was written and committed before anything is scored. We build nothing if 8 or more of 10 real questions find their answer in the top 5 results. We build only if at least 3 misses are sitting at ranks 6–20, and even then memsearch's free built-in reranker gets tried first. I'm waiting on the question set, then I'll run the test.

"""Print the top results for the missed questions, to audit the scorer by eye."""

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

questions = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
wanted = {int(x) for x in sys.argv[2].split(",")}
for q in questions:
    if q["id"] not in wanted:
        continue
    out = subprocess.run(["memsearch", "search", q["question"], "-k", "20", "-j"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    print(f"== {q['id']}: {q['question'][:70]}")
    keys = [k.lower() for k in q["answer_keywords"]]
    for i, r in enumerate(json.loads(out.stdout), start=1):
        src = r["source"].replace("\\", "/").split(".claude/")[-1]
        hits = sum(1 for k in keys if k in r["content"].lower())
        print(f"  {i:>2} {r['score']:.3f} kw{hits}/{len(keys)} {src[-80:]}")

Questions: `rerank_measure/questions.json`, 10 real prompts from 2026-08-30 to
2026-09-20, collected newest-first by a subagent with no memsearch access. Scorer:
`rerank_measure/score.py`. Audit of the misses: `rerank_measure/inspect_misses.py`.

| id | question (short) | strict | audited |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | next tasks for Jev? | miss@20 | **rank 17** (closeout handoff; the answer changed since, so the keywords missed it) |
| 2 | next use cases from the handoff doc | miss@20 | miss@20, **context-dependent** |

| 10 | CFBD and Perch pipelines? | 3 | 3 |

**hit@5 is 4 of 10 strict, 5 of 10 audited. Misses in ranks 6 to 20: 1 strict, 2
audited.** The rule needed 3, so no reranker, and the local cross-encoder trial does
not trigger either. Retrieval is weak, but a reranker is the wrong fix, because it
cannot reorder what never comes back:

- **3 of the 6 misses are questions that do not name their subject** ("these outputs",
  "the handoff doc"). Every result scores a flat ~0.5, so there is no signal to rank.
  The fix is query formation: the agent should rewrite the question with the
  conversation's subject before calling memsearch. That is a line in the
  `memory-write` retrieval ladder, not a model.
- **1 is coverage**: `graphify-out/RESUME.md` is not indexed.
- **1 is dilution**: "Jev" pulls the 59 mirrored vendor pages
  (`dev-docs/TypeSafe_Sandbox/vendor/`) into ranks 1 to 3 ahead of project state.
  Excluding `vendor/` from the index is a code fix.

All three fixes are code or instructions, which is gate condition 3 doing its job.

Limits worth stating: 10 questions; 7 of 10 were found by reading prompts by hand
rather than by regex; three answers changed after they were asked (1, 6, 8), and
questions 1 and 9 were re-scored by eye in the audit column.

content.text:
I ran the `rerank_typesafe` test against the rule I committed before scoring, and it says **don't build it**. That makes five Jev ideas in a row that measurement has ruled out.

**The numbers:** 4 of 10 real past questions found their answer in the top 5 results, or 5 of 10 after I checked the misses by hand. A reranker only helps when the answer sits at ranks 6–20, and at most 2 did. The rule needed at least 3, so memsearch's own free reranker didn't get tried either.

**Why search misses, and none of it needs Jev:**
- **3 of the 6 misses were questions like "where are these outputs?"** They don't name their subject, so search has nothing to go on. The fix is for Claude to add the subject from the conversation before it searches. That's one line in the `memory-write` skill.
- **One answer file was never indexed** (`graphify-out/`).
- **For "next tasks for Jev?", the copied TypeSafe product docs took the top 3 spots** because they match the word "Jev"; today's actual answer came 17th. The fix is to leave those docs out of the search index.

All three are in `STATUS.md` under Next.

**Your other points:**
- **#2 (import command):** from this prompt, with Zotero open: `! cd ~/Desktop/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox && python verifier/tos_sources/import_to_zotero.py --pmid 38707577`. That's a dry run; add `--go` to actually import. Then check the PDF is attached to the item, and I'll do the rest.
- **#3 (verifier):** the send gate already existed. What I found was a bug: a review with no Zotero key, which is #002's state, was reported as "a claim does not match the paper".     tables = re.findall(r"Table [IVX]+", text)
    has = [v for v in ("37.2", "126.2", "91.1", "7.3") if v in text]
    print(n, "62x tokens:", nums[:6], "| tables:", sorted(set(tables)), "| values:", has)

def body_pages(pages: dict[int, str]) -> dict[int, str]:
    """The paper with its apparatus removed: bibliography, markers, running header.

    Presence of a figure is only evidence when the figure could have come from the
    prose. Reference markers, the bibliography's years and page ranges, and the DOI
    in the page banner are all digits that say nothing about what the paper claims,
    and together they make every integer 0-37 "present" in paper 001.

    Used for the NUMERIC PRESENCE checks only. The model path still reads the full
    page text, because a claim may legitimately be about a declaration or a figure
    caption, and because that path's false-alarm behaviour was measured on the
    untouched text and is not worth disturbing to solve a different problem.
    """
    header = _running_header(pages)
    cut_page, cut_at = None, None
    for page, text in sorted(pages.items()):
        for match in REFERENCES_HEAD.finditer(normalize(text)):
            cut_page, cut_at = page, match.start()

    body: dict[int, str] = {}
    for page, text in sorted(pages.items()):
        text = normalize(text)
        if cut_page is not None:
            if page > cut_page:
                text = ""               # wholly bibliography and author affiliations
            elif page == cut_page:
                text = text[:cut_at]
        if header:
            text = text.replace(header, " ")
        body[page] = CITATION_MARKER.sub(" ", text)
    return body


def find_number_word(pages: dict[int, str], value: str) -> list[int]:
    """Every page that spells this integer out as a word.

    PROSE ONLY, and integers only - no paper writes a standard deviation as a word.
    Runs alongside `find_number_rounded`, never instead of it: a figure is absent
    only when neither the digits nor the word appear.
    """
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return []
    if number != int(number):
        return []
    word = next((name for name, digit in _WORD_TO_NUMBER.items()
                 if digit == int(number)), None)
    if word is None:
        return []
    pattern = re.compile(rf"\b{word}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    return [
        page for page, text in sorted(pages.items())
        if pattern.search(dehyphenate(text))
    ]


def words(text: str) -> set[str]:
    return {
        word for word in re.findall(r"[a-z]{3,}", text.lower())
        if word not in STOPWORDS
    }


def best_page(pages: dict[int, str], text: str) -> tuple[int | None, float]:
    """The page with most keyword overlap with this claim, and the overlap fraction.

    Deliberately in code and before any call. Sending all 11 pages would blow the
    state budget, and sending the wrong page is the documented context-rot failure:
    accuracy falls as the state fills with irrelevant text.
    """
    needle = words(text)
    if not needle:
        return None, 0.0
    best, score = None, 0.0
    for page, page_text in sorted(pages.items()):
        overlap = len(needle & words(page_text)) / len(needle)
        if overlap > score:
            best, score = page, overlap
    return best, score


def _self_test() -> None:
    """The number scanner's edge cases, runnable without the database."""
    cases = [
        ("the sample was 22.", 22.0, True),      # sentence-final: must be found
        ("83.89° ±1.78°", 1.78, True),           # glued to a degree sign
        ("88.00° ± 2.62°", 88.0, True),          # 88.00 in the paper, 88.0 in the deck
        ("mean 41.783", 1.78, False),            # not a number inside another
        ("the 22nd player", 22.0, False),        # not a number inside a word
        ("it was 22.5 degrees", 22.0, False),    # not the integer part of a decimal
        ("P = 0.277", 0.277, True),
    ]
    failures = 0
    for text, target, expected in cases:
        got = target in numbers_on(normalize(text))
        mark = "ok " if got == expected else "FAIL"
        if got != expected:
            failures += 1
        print(f"  [{mark}] {target!r:>8} {'in' if expected else 'not in'} {text!r}")

    # The apparatus strippers and the word matcher, on strings rather than a paper.
    # The de-hyphenation case is the one that earns its keep: without it the number
    # word "ten" is found inside "ten<soft hyphen> derness" and a paper that never
    # says ten reports it present.
    broken = "localized ten­ derness (right)"
    text_cases = [
        ("dehyphenate rejoins a broken word",
         "ten" not in re.findall(r"\b[a-z]+\b", dehyphenate(broken))),
        ("dehyphenate keeps the word itself",
         "tenderness" in dehyphenate(broken)),
        ("bare 'ten' would match before dehyphenating",
         bool(re.search(r"\bten\b", broken))),
        ("citation markers take their digits with them",
         not re.search(r"\d", CITATION_MARKER.sub(
             " ", "role [27]. Also [3, 4] and [1-3]."))),
        ("a bare bracket is not a citation",
         CITATION_MARKER.sub(" ", "the [n] case") == "the [n] case"),
        ("word lookup maps 7 to seven",
         find_number_word({1: "Seven coronal plane angles"}, "7") == [1]),
        ("word lookup is integers only",
         find_number_word({1: "seven point five"}, "7.5") == []),
        ("word lookup does not match a substring",
         find_number_word({1: "the seventh angle"}, "7") == []),
        # The first version of the header finder anchored on page 1 and returned ""
        # on every real paper, stripping nothing while the docs claimed otherwise.
        # A title page with its own furniture ahead of the banner is the normal case,
        # not the exception, so it is the case worth pinning.
        ("running header survives a different title page",
         _running_header({
             1: "RESEARCH | Journal of Examples 2026 Title of the paper",
             2: "Journal of Examples 2026 Introduction text here",
             3: "Journal of Examples 2026 Methods text here",
             4: "Journal of Examples 2026 Results text here",
         }) == "Journal of Examples 2026"),
        ("no header when pages share no banner",
         _running_header({1: "Alpha one", 2: "Beta two",
                          3: "Gamma three", 4: "Delta four"}) == ""),
    ]
    for label, passed in text_cases:
        if not passed:
            failures += 1
        print(f"  [{'ok ' if passed else 'FAIL'}] {label}")

    print("  all source cases pass" if not failures
          else f"  {failures} FAILED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

        _self_test()
